body: (And I would add most other files in `~/.config/syncthing` should probably rather end up in `~/.local/share/syncthing`)

As described in #9178, I think even `$XDG_DATA_HOME` would not be the ideal placement.  Not authoritative, but https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/XDG_Base_Directory#User_directories describes it as analogous to `/usr/share`, which as the name implies, could be shared between devices.  Sharing the configuration files, e.g. device ID certificate, would be problematic though.
If there's a log file there it's because you manually asked for it, we don't default to using any log file on unixes.

That is why there is a /usr/**local**/share on your system. XDG has a ~/.local too.
That's an implementation detail of the leveldb database and not what the OP is talking about.

> That is why there is a /usr/local/share on your system. XDG has a ~/.local too.

The XDG Base Directory Specification is not really related to the LSB Filesystem Hierarchy Standard (FHS).  In contrast to the latter, it is very vague on what goes where and what could possibly be shared between different machines.  The name `.local` MAY imply that it should be kept local to the machine, but the standard makes no such statement.  And the `share` part does suggest to me that it is intended to be shared.

Regarding the FHS and the `/usr/local/` hierarchy, the distinction is basically between stuff managed by the distribution through its package system (`/usr/`) and stuff added by the local administrator.  It has nothing to do with `~/.local/`.

Indeed, that's being set in our own `etc/linux-desktop/syncthing-start.desktop` file.  Should we treat it as a bug to be fixed in that file?

Anyhow, when fixing #9178, the default log file location should be moved as well.
